title: Rigveda 5.64: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.64: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.64 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 384r-385r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.64.1-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 2); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 384v
translation.original_text:
1varu̍ṇaṁ vo ri̱śāda̍sam ṛ̱cā mi̱traṁ ha̍vāmahe | pari̍ vra̱jeva̍ bā̱hvor ja̍ga̱nvāṁsā̱ sva̍rṇaram ||
2tā bā̱havā̍ suce̱tunā̱ pra ya̍ntam asmā̱ arca̍te | śeva̱ṁ hi jā̱rya̍ṁ vā̱ṁ viśvā̍su̱ kṣāsu̱ jogu̍ve ||
3yan nū̱nam a̱śyāṁ gati̍m mi̱trasya̍ yāyām pa̱thā | asya̍ pri̱yasya̱ śarma̱ṇy ahi̍ṁsānasya saścire ||
4yu̱vābhyā̍m mitrāvaruṇopa̱maṁ dhe̍yām ṛ̱cā | yad dha̱ kṣaye̍ ma̱ghonā̍ṁ stotṝ̱ṇāṁ ca̍ spū̱rdhase̍ ||
5ā no̍ mitra sudī̱tibhi̱r varu̍ṇaś ca sa̱dhastha̱ ā | sve kṣaye̍ ma̱ghonā̱ṁ sakhī̍nāṁ ca vṛ̱dhase̍ ||
translation.text:
1You, foeman-slaying Varuṇa and Mitra, we invoke with song, Who, as with penfold of your arms, encompass round the realm of light.
2Stretch out your arms with favouring love unto this man who singeth hymns, For in all places is sung forth your evergracious friendliness.
3That I may gain a refuge now, may my steps be on Mitra's path. Men go protected in the charge of this dear Friend who harms us not.
4Mitra and Varuṇa, from you may I, by song, win noblest meed. That shall stir envy in the homes of wealthy chiefs and those who praise.
5With your fair splendours, Varuṇa and Mitra, to our gathering come, That in their homes the wealthy chiefs and they who are your friends may thrive.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 384v (numbered 57v by the scribe) (OPenn image 385, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.64.1 ‹havāmahe pari vrajāiva bāhvoḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 385r (numbered 58r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.64.6 ‹-vāja-sātaye kṛtam rāye svastaye›. Verses 5.64.1-5 end on this page; 5.64.1 begins on fol. 384r (numbered 57r by the scribe).

1varuṇam | vaḥ | riśādasam | ṛcā | mitram | havāmahe | pari | vrajāiva | bāhvoḥ | jaganvāṃsā | svaḥ-naram
2tā | bāhavā | su-cetunā | pra | yantam | asmai | arcate | śevam | hi | jāryam | vām | vi śvāsu | kṣāsu | joguve
3yat | nūnam | aśyām | gatim | mitrasya | yāyām | pathā | asya | priyasya | śarmaṇ i | ahiṃsānasya | saścire
4yuvābhyām | mitrāvaruṇā | upa-mam | dheyām | ṛcā | yat | ha | kṣaye | maghonām | stotṝṇām | ca | spūrdhase
5ā | naḥ | mitra | sudīti-bhiḥ | varuṇaḥ | ca | sadha-sthe | ā | sve | kṣaye | maghonām | sakhīnām | ca | vṛdhase

translation.original_ref: RV 5.64.6-7 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 2); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 385r
translation.original_text:
6yu̱vaṁ no̱ yeṣu̍ varuṇa kṣa̱tram bṛ̱hac ca̍ bibhṛ̱thaḥ | u̱ru ṇo̱ vāja̍sātaye kṛ̱taṁ rā̱ye sva̱staye̍ ||
7u̱cchantyā̍m me yaja̱tā de̱vakṣa̍tre̱ ruśa̍dgavi | su̱taṁ soma̱ṁ na ha̱stibhi̱r ā pa̱ḍbhir dhā̍vataṁ narā̱ bibhra̍tāv arca̱nāna̍sam ||
translation.text:
6With those, moreover, among whom ye hold your high supremacy, Vouchsafe us room that we may win strength for prosperity and wealth.
7When morning flushes, Holy Ones! in the Gods' realm where white Cows shine, Supporting Archanânas, speed, ye Heroes, with your active feet hither to my pressed Soma juice.
